metadata.title: Palantir: Khan contract ban will cut Met police jobs

content.text:
Palantir has claimed that Sir Sadiq Khan's contract ban will lead to the Metropolitan Police cutting frontline jobs.
In submissions to the High Court, the US tech giant said the Mayor of London's decision to block its £50m contract will prevent the Met from working more efficiently, meaning it will be forced to reduce costs elsewhere.
The claims were made as Palantir sought to overturn Sir Sadiq's decision to cancel its two-year partnership with the Met.
The company claimed the Mayor unlawfully blocked the contract because he objected to the tech company's "ethics". This was based on its work for the Israeli military and the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (Ice).
Palantir's challenge was supported by submissions to the High Court from the Met, which said that Sir Sadiq's decision will lead to "unpalatable additional cuts to significant frontline policing services".
The Met said Palantir's project, which was aimed at using AI for analysis in criminal investigations, would have lowered costs "through the automation of routine and repetitive tasks".
The Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (Mopac) said it cancelled the contract because of a "clear and serious breach" of procurement rules, claiming that the Met had only considered Palantir for the contract.
In an interview with LBC in June, Sir Mark Rowley, the head of the Met, said the force wanted to use Palantir's technology to "automate some of our bureaucratic processes" and for "faster analytics to help officers investigating crime".
Sir Mark said the decision to scrap Palantir's contract would force the Metropolitan Police to make "tough choices that affect the quality of policing in London".
Palantir said the Mayor's decision also risks having "broader adverse commercial consequences" for its own business and deter it from engaging with other public bodies.
The filings said: "[Palantir] is concerned that other potential contractors may be influenced or emboldened by the Mopac decision to reject Palantir or exclude Palantir from other public contracts on the basis of similar impermissible or improper reasons."
It comes as ministers are also reviewing whether to use a break clause to cancel Palantir's contract with the NHS, two years into its seven-year deal, with a decision due by December.
The Government has faced calls from Labour MPs and unions to block Palantir from public sector work, while Andy Burnham has signalled he would scrap the tech giant's £330m contract with the health service.
Zack Polanski, the Green Party leader, has also urged the Government to "cut Palantir out of our NHS".
